name: Sphinx, Threskisphinx
body:
Threskisphinx
CR 8

This creature has a lean leonine body, nearly hairless save for its tufted tail. Its head and neck resemble a dark-feathered ibis with a massive bill, while a pair of strong, white wings sprout from its shoulders.

XP 4,800
NG Large magical beast
Init +2; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +20

DEFENSE

AC 21, touch 11, flat-footed 19 (+2 Dex, +10 natural, –1 size)
hp 95 (10d10+40)
Fort +11, Ref +9, Will +10

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., fly 60 ft. (poor)
Melee bite +14 (2d8+5/19–20 plus grab), 2 claws +14 (2d6+5)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks rake (2 claws +14, 2d6+5)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 10th; concentration +14)

At will—goodberry, guidance, resistance
3/day—entangle (DC 15), produce flame
1/day—call lightning (DC 18), dimension door (self only), flaming sphere (DC 17), freedom of movement, ice storm, lesser geas (DC 18), plant growth, sound burst (DC 17)

STATISTICS

Str 20, Dex 15, Con 18, Int 17, Wis 24, Cha 19
Base Atk +10; CMB +16 (+20 grapple); CMD 28 (32 vs. trip)
Feats Combat Casting, Flyby Attack, Improved Critical (bite), Skill Focus (Knowledge [nature]), Spell Focus (evocation)
Skills Fly +9, Intimidate +14, Knowledge (any one) +13, Knowledge (nature) +19, Perception +20
Languages Common, Sphinx, Sylvan

ECOLOGY

Environment warm hills or urban
Organization solitary or pair
Treasure standard

Among the rarest of their kind, these ibis-headed sphinxes are legendary for their knowledge, wisdom, and skill at working magic. They tend to dwell near lakes, marshes, wetlands, and reedy riverine backwaters, hiding among and even protecting flocks of waterbirds who dwell nearby.

They can be kindly but are taciturn and dislike uninvited guests, often simply departing rather than engaging in conversation or—if those guests prove rude—chastising or chasing them away with magic, threats, or direct attacks as a last resort. They eat only small fish and marsh crustaceans, so they have no hunger for sentient flesh and prefer to avoid physical confrontation but may unleash their fury if driven to extremes.

Magical Craft

Threskisphinxes sometimes apply the power of their magical knowledge to create enchanted relics and items, sometimes merely as an academic curiosity but others because of some foretelling of future need. Those seeking the aid of these creatures may go to them for wisdom, but they also may look for more direct and practical aid in the form of requesting a gift (or at least the loan) of an item the threskisphinx has crafted. Each sphinx manufactures only a few mystically imbued items, so they do not gift them lightly, but if persuaded by the need at hand may grant their use to heroes that prove themselves worthy.
